findings.name: cryptography
findings.provides_note: PROVIDES these algorithms. This is reachability, not use: no call site, mode, key size or protocol is established here.
findings.capability_note: Python's primary crypto provider; `hazmat` is a low-level bindings surface.
findings.capability_gate: PQC is version-gated (ML-DSA/SLH-DSA from 45.0, ML-KEM from 46.0). A bare pin proves neither, so no PQC claim is asserted here

policy_deadline.label: NIST IR 8547 ipd -- quantum-vulnerable PKC (DRAFT)
policy_deadline.note: No SP 800-57 equivalent security strength could be determined, so no tier could be selected. NOT counted as compliant and NOT deprecated.

assumptions: Y=4.0y from artefact_class='library': third-party / vendored dependency upgrade
Z=20.0y is a CRQC estimate, not a compliance deadline (policy deadline: 2035)

recommendation.algorithm: Inventory as dependency; migrate consumers per artefact
recommendation.action: Record the library and assess consumers, not the library itself
recommendation.justification: This finding records the PRESENCE of a cryptography provider, not the USE of an algorithm. A library implements many algorithms (`implements`, not `uses`); the migration unit is each consumer's actual call. Nothing in a library finding alone implies breakage.
recommendation.rule_trace: RULE-LIB: primitive=cryptographic-library -> inventory dependency; assess `uses` edges

never_in_scope: transitive dependencies (absent from the manifest; resolving them means running the package manager, which this tool refuses to do)
dynamic / plugin / runtime-loaded providers not named in any manifest
the algorithm set of a LIBRARY that wraps a system library (openssl, Node `crypto`, native-tls): that is a property of the linked binary, not the pin
vendored source trees not described by a manifest we recognise
coverage.assurance: capability -- a dependency makes an algorithm REACHABLE. No finding in this sensor proves a call site.
